strategy.summary: GET /products (src/app.js listProducts) filters the catalogue by a case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages with `limit` (default DEFAULT_LIMIT=20, capped at MAX_LIMIT=50) and `offset` (default 0), returns {total, items}, and answers 400 when limit/offset aren't whole numbers (regex ^\d+$) or limit < 1. Tests start the real app in-process on an OS-chosen port, as the existing suite does, and prove search, paging, the cap and each refusal.
inScope: GET /products query parameters q, limit, offset
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
Shop search box UI (not in this repository)
assumptions: The real app runs in-process via createApp() on port 0, nothing is faked; expectations are derived from the exported PRODUCTS catalogue, DEFAULT_LIMIT and MAX_LIMIT rather than hard-coded copies where possible.
'Capped' means a limit above MAX_LIMIT (50) returns MAX_LIMIT items with status 200, not a refusal, as the code does.
A negative number or an empty value counts as 'not a whole number' and is refused with 400, as the code does; offset 0 is valid.
Items are returned in catalogue order (by id), which the code does; paging assertions rely on it.
openQuestions: Should an offset beyond the last match return 200 with empty items (current behaviour) or be refused? Tested as 200 with empty items and the real total.

risks.description: Search is case-sensitive or matches only prefixes, so shoppers miss products
risks.mitigation: TC1 uses mixed case; TC2 matches a substring inside names

risks.description: total reports the page size instead of all matches, breaking pagination UI
risks.mitigation: TC3, TC5, TC6, TC7 assert total independently of the page length

risks.description: Unbounded limit lets a client fetch huge pages
Malformed paging params cause 500s or silently wrong pages
risks.mitigation: TC9-TC11 assert 400 for each kind of bad value

acceptanceCriteria.text: q returns only products whose name contains q, case-insensitively; without q every product is listed.
Results are paged with limit and offset, the response includes the total number of matches, and limits above the maximum are capped.
A limit or offset that isn't a whole number, or a limit below 1, is refused with status 400.

testCases.title: matches product names regardless of the case of q
preconditions: App listening on an OS-chosen port
testCases.expected: 200; total 15; items are exactly the PRODUCTS whose lower-cased name contains 'kettle' (Kettle 1..15), in catalogue order
testCases.rationale: Core search behaviour and case insensitivity

testCases.title: matches q anywhere in the name, not only at the start
testCases.expected: 200; total 15; every item is a Teapot N product, matching the PRODUCTS filtered by name containing 'pot'

testCases.title: lists every product when q is absent
testCases.expected: 200; total equals PRODUCTS.length (120); items are the first DEFAULT_LIMIT products

testCases.title: returns no items and a total of 0 when nothing matches q
returns the page selected by limit and offset with the total of all matches
testCases.expected: 200; total 120; items are products with ids 11-15

testCases.title: pages through search results with total counting all matches
testCases.expected: 200; total 15; items are Mug 2 and Mug 3

testCases.title: caps a limit above the maximum at MAX_LIMIT items
testCases.expected: 200; items length MAX_LIMIT (50), the first 50 products; total 120

testCases.title: returns an empty page and the real total when offset is past the last match
testCases.rationale: Boundary at the end of results

testCases.title: refuses a limit below 1 with 400 and accepts a limit of 1
testCases.expected: limit=0 -> 400 with an error body; limit=1 -> 200 with exactly one item

testCases.title: refuses a limit that is not a whole number with 400
steps: For each of 1.5, abc, -5, empty string: GET /products?limit=<value> (URL-encoded)

testCases.title: refuses an offset that is not a whole number with 400
steps: For each of 1.5, abc, -1, empty string: GET /products?offset=<value> (URL-encoded)

strategy.environmentNotes: No external services. The app is started in-process with createApp().listen(0) per test file and closed in afterAll; the existing `npm test` (vitest run) picks up the new file.
